summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a complex history including Crohn’s disease, short bowel syndrome, SVC repair, and HIT was readmitted with bloody diarrhea, fever, and vomiting. She had recently completed a course of levofloxacin for pneumonia. Evaluation supported a Crohn’s flare, with elevated inflammatory markers and negative stool studies for infection. She was managed with ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. Due to extensive venous occlusive disease, IV access was lost and could not be reestablished, prompting a transition to oral and rectal medications. Given her severe anxiety and PTSD, she elected for early discharge after tolerating oral hydromorphone and rectal promethazine. She was discharged home on antibiotics, analgesics, and continued fondaparinux, with close follow-up advised.
